theme: Injection and unsafe input handling in a small ASP.NET Core report-builder and document-search API

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The search term from the request is interpolated inside a quoted ILIKE literal of a raw SQL string handed to Dapper. A term containing a quote closes the literal and appends arbitrary SQL (`x%' UNION SELECT ... --`). Dapper binds nothing here because the value is already part of the text.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The owner filter, taken from the query string, is interpolated into a SQL string that is then passed to EF Core's FromSqlRaw. Building the string first and passing a plain string defeats EF's interpolation protection (FromSqlRaw does no parameterisation of text it is given).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The saved-search name from the route is concatenated into the CommandText of an NpgsqlCommand: `x' OR '1'='1` deletes every saved search of the owner, and stacked statements run with the service's database role.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The export format chosen by the caller is spliced into a `/bin/sh -c` command line. The request model only requires the field to be non-empty, so `pdf; curl ...` or `$( ... )` runs as the service account.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The attachment file name from the route is joined onto the storage root with Path.Combine and opened with no canonicalisation or containment check: `..%2F..%2Fappsettings.Production.json` (or an absolute path, which makes Path.Combine discard the root) reads any file the process can read.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The import preview fetches whatever URL the caller supplies, from inside the network, and returns the response's status, content type, size and Last-Modified: http://169.254.169.254/ metadata, localhost admin ports and internal hosts are all reachable. Nothing checks scheme, host or resolved address.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The webhook address check unwraps IPv4-mapped IPv6 and rejects private IPv4 ranges, but treats every other IPv6 address outside the link-local/site-local/ULA/loopback prefixes as public. The same internal host written as NAT64 (64:ff9b::a00:1), 6to4 (2002:a00:1::) or IPv4-compatible (::10.0.0.1) is classified public; on a NAT64 network (common for IPv6-only clusters) the first form connects straight to 10.0.0.1, so a tenant can register a callback that reaches internal services.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Uploaded metadata XML is loaded into an XmlDocument whose XmlResolver is explicitly set to an XmlUrlResolver, so a DOCTYPE with an external entity (`<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` or an http URL) is resolved and its content lands in the imported metadata.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The field name from the route is concatenated into an XPath predicate that is meant to hide restricted fields: `x' or @restricted='true' or 'a'='b` rewrites the predicate and returns every restricted field.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Imported saved-search files (uploaded by users) are deserialized with Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling.All into a model whose Parameters dictionary holds `object` values, so a `$type` in the file instantiates any type on the probing path (the classic gadget chains), i.e. remote code execution on a payload the caller controls.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The empty-result widget echoes the raw query parameter into a text/html response that the archive front end inserts into its page: `?q=` is reflected cross-site scripting.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Values read out of the uploaded metadata XML (XmlNode.InnerText) are written into a quoted HTML attribute and element text without encoding. The document's author controls the value, so `" onmouseover="...` closes the attribute and adds script to the preview every reader of the document opens.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: After an export is queued the caller is redirected to the returnUrl query parameter with no check, so a link to this trusted host can bounce users to any site (phishing a login page that looks like the archive).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The e-mail address the caller searches for is concatenated into an LDAP filter without RFC 4515 escaping: `*)(objectClass=*` widens the search to every entry and leaks directory attributes back through the owner lookup.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The highlight pattern is supplied by the caller and compiled with the backtracking engine and no match timeout, then run over whole document texts: `(a+)+$` against a long run of `a`s pins a request thread indefinitely.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Passwords that protect share links are stored as an unsalted MD5 digest. MD5 is fast and unsalted digests are precomputed, so a leaked shares table yields the passwords in seconds; a password needs a slow, salted KDF (PBKDF2, bcrypt, Argon2).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Every delivery writes the subscriber's e-mail address to the information log (a source-generated LoggerMessage whose template carries {EmailAddress}), which is shipped to the log platform and kept far longer than the subscription; the subscriber id already identifies the delivery.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The subscriber's e-mail address is sent to the CRM in the query string of a GET request, so it is written to the CRM's and every proxy's access logs; the CRM also accepts the address in a POST body.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Each entry of an uploaded bundle file starts with a 32-bit length that is passed straight to ReadBytes / used to size the buffer: a 12-byte file claiming a 2 GB entry makes the server allocate it (and a negative length throws deep in the reader). The length is never compared to the remaining stream or a limit.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The public Flatten(XElement) walks the uploaded metadata tree by recursing into every child element with no depth limit; XML parsing imposes none, so a document nested a few hundred thousand levels deep overflows the stack, which in .NET kills the process instead of failing the request.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Dapper query with a named parameter (`@Id` bound from an anonymous object): the value never becomes SQL text.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An interpolated SQL string, but both holes come from code: the column is looked up in a fixed dictionary of column names (unknown keys fall back to a constant) and the direction is one of two literals. The caller selects; it never supplies text. Identifiers cannot be bound as parameters, so this is the correct pattern.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: EF Core FromSqlInterpolated turns each interpolation hole into a DbParameter; the interpolated syntax is what makes it safe.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: NpgsqlCommand with a constant CommandText and every value added through Parameters.AddWithValue.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A fixed executable path (configuration, never the request) started with UseShellExecute=false, every value passed as its own ArgumentList element: the size comes from a defined enum and both paths are absolute paths the service generated, so none can begin with a dash. No shell parses anything and no value can add or split arguments.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The template name is combined with the root, canonicalised with Path.GetFullPath and rejected unless the result is still inside the root (StartsWith root + separator, ordinal); `..` sequences and absolute paths are refused before the file is opened.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The partner feed URL comes from the request but is only fetched if it is https and its host is one of the configured partner hosts (exact, case-insensitive match); anything else is refused before a request is made.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A hand-written address check that unwraps IPv4-mapped IPv6 and rejects private IPv4 ranges like the webhook one, but refuses EVERY other IPv6 address (partner endpoints are IPv4-only). 6to4, NAT64 and IPv4-compatible forms are native IPv6 and are therefore rejected; there is no embedding to walk past.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: XmlReader.Create with DtdProcessing.Prohibit and a null XmlResolver: a document with a DOCTYPE is rejected, so neither external nor internal entities are processed.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: XPath built by concatenation, but the section name was verified with XmlConvert.VerifyNCName first: an NCName cannot contain `/`, `[`, `'`, `(` or whitespace, so it can only name one child element.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Newtonsoft settings for report layouts set TypeNameHandling.None explicitly (and MaxDepth): `$type` in the payload is ignored and only the declared layout types are created.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The results widget writes document titles into HTML through HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode; the encoded text cannot open a tag or close an attribute.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A value read from the document XML is HTML-encoded before it is written into a quoted attribute.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The page count comes from the document XML but is parsed to a non-negative int (NumberStyles.None, invariant culture) before it is formatted into the attribute; digits cannot break out of it.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The return URL is followed only if Url.IsLocalUrl accepts it (a path on this host, not `//evil` or `/\evil`), via LocalRedirect; otherwise the caller lands on a fixed page.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A filter built by concatenation, but the value is passed through an RFC 4515 escaper (`*`, `(`, `)`, `\` and NUL become \2a, \28, \29, \5c, \00) so it can only ever be an attribute value.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A constant, anchored pattern with no nested quantifiers, compiled once with a 100 ms match timeout; only the input is user-supplied, never the pattern.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: MD5 used to derive an HTTP ETag for cache validation of rendered previews. No security property depends on it: a collision only makes a cache revalidate wrongly for content the caller could already read.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A bounce is logged with a keyed HMAC of the address (emailAddressHash, from EmailPseudonymizer), the stable pseudonymous reference GDPR guidance recommends; the address itself is not logged.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: `email=` in this query string is a boolean channel switch (`email=true|false`) addressed by an opaque subscription id; no personal data is in the URL.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The index entry's name length is read from the file, but it is rejected unless 0 < length <= 1024 before ReadBytes is called.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Recursion over a JsonNode filter tree without its own depth counter, but every JsonNode it receives comes from System.Text.Json (request body binding or JsonNode.Parse), whose reader refuses documents nested deeper than MaxDepth (64 by default); the recursion is therefore bounded at 64 frames.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: CA2007 (ConfigureAwait) is switched off at the repository root with its reason on the line above: tests must not call ConfigureAwait(false) (xUnit1030), and src/.editorconfig switches it back on as a warning for all production code. A scoped, documented suppression is good practice, not hidden debt. Promoted from a scanner false positive in scan iteration 1 (the same site is TRP-001 in bench-csharp-baseline-clean).

entries.rationale: Nothing is evaluated as code: no scripting engine, no dynamic compilation, no server-side template engine (HTML snippets are built from strings, which is measured as cross-site scripting).

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: JWT bearer authentication, five scope policies, an authenticated-user fallback policy and [Authorize] with a named policy on every controller; only the health check and the password-protected share landing page are anonymous.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: The service holds personal data (subscriber and owner e-mail addresses, in a database it owns) and enforces HTTPS, but nothing is encrypted at rest, no key vault or data-protection API is used, and the only password store is unsalted MD5 (HASH-001). Weak posture, not absent transport security.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Every request model carries data annotations under [ApiController], so validation exists, but it checks presence and length only: the fields that reach SQL, a shell, the file system, outbound requests, LDAP, regex and redirects are not constrained. Read as the web-security posture as a whole, transport and headers are good while MD5 password hashing and personal data in an outbound URL pull it down. Middling.
